newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates remain high, activity muted.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates remain high, activity muted.

text.p: Dutch call money rates remained at a relatively high level on Monday and dealers said some market players might still be unfamiliar with the new instruments introduced in May by the central bank.
"One player had to make use of the new marginal advance facility last Friday," said one dealer, explaining that liquidity was not evenly divided among participants.
Banks that are short of liquidity at the end of the day have to obtain overnight credit from the central bank at the marginal advances rate, which is currently set at 4.50 percent.
Commercial banks are no longer allowed to show a debit balance on their cash reserve account at the central bank at the end of a trading day.
"Call money rates are high because participants are still unfamiliar with the new instruments," said one dealer.
He said the participant who had to obtain liquidity through the marginal advance facility was only two million guilders short.
Call money was bid at 3.18 percent on Monday against 3.12 percent on Friday, while the special advances rate has been pegged at 2.90 percent since March.
The special advances rate sets the tone for money market rates.
Deposits were stable, with one month paper trading at an unchanged 3.18 percent and three-month deposits at 3.20 percent.
The guilder was virtually unchanged at 112.495 per 100 marks from 112.50 on Friday.
